Gold holds gains, silver slips as Wall Street plunges, Fed hike bets ease - Kitco PM Report
items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) - Spot gold prices were higher and spot silver prices were lower in late U.S. trading Thursday, as a sharp technology-led equity market selloff drove Treasury yields lower and reduced expectations for additional Federal Reserve tightening in December. Renewed attacks on commercial shipping near the Strait of Hormuz pushed crude oil prices higher, reversing part of Wednesday's steep decline and adding to uncertainty surrounding the inflation outlook. Gold retained much of its post-election recovery as investors sought defensive assets, while silver surrendered earlier gains amid heavy selling across technology and industrially sensitive markets. At the latest verified afternoon quotation, spot gold was trading near $4,087.26 an ounce, up $25.93, or 0.64%, while spot silver was trading near $51.778, down $0.407, or 0.78%, on the session. Gold had earlier reached $4,148.00, its highest intraday level since Oct. 20, before retreating as the equity selloff intensified. Thursday's U.S. economic reports pointed to stronger labor productivity and moderating wage-related inflation pressure, while initial jobless claims indicated that layoffs remain limited. Nonfarm business productivity increased at a 3.6% annualized rate in the third quarter, above expectations for a 2.8% gain and accelerating from an upwardly revised 2.1% in the second quarter. Output increased 3.7%, while hours worked edged up 0.1%. Unit labor costs declined at a 0.7% annualized rate, compared with expectations for a 0.6% increase, reversing the previous quarter's revised 1.9% rise. The decline suggests that stronger productivity is helping businesses absorb compensation increases without equivalent increases in production costs, potentially reducing one source of underlying inflation pressure.

items.titleEn: World Bank sees gold holding above $4,000 through 2028, but warns silver faces steeper correction
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - Gold and silver prices are expected to remain historically elevated through 2027, but investors should not expect a repeat of the explosive gains and volatility that defined 2026, according to the latest report from the World Bank. In its October Commodity Markets Outlook, analysts at the World Bank forecast gold prices to average $4,600 an ounce this year, a 33.6% increase from 2025. However, the bank expects prices to fall 7.6% to an average of $4,250 an ounce in 2027, followed by a further 5.9% decline to $4,000 in 2028. The outlook is slightly more bearish than the bank's April forecast, which projected gold prices averaging $4,700 this year and $4,300 in 2027.
